title: Sunday · Cedar, xii · just the mill
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · from 2017 the aggregator
logline: The last of twelve. The mill as it is. No branch from the stack, no hedge, no blade in the sky. Chain-link, rust, alders through the boards. The phantom novel closes. The strip draws what's there, and it's enough.

panels.composition: Tier 1: the mill from the road, exactly as it is: chain-link, padlock, blackberry, the brick stack bare against an August sky. No magic anywhere.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rust, a shuttered mill seen from a road exactly as it is with a chain-link gate and padlock and blackberry and a bare brick smokestack against an August sky, no words

panels.name: As it is

panels.composition: Tier 2: WOOD at the gate with BARNABY II, looking through. The real gate. His hand on the real wire.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rust, a man with his hand on a real chain-link gate looking through it at a mill yard, a small three-legged dog beside him, no words

panels.name: The wire

panels.composition: Tier 3: the yard through the gate. The alders through the boards, forty feet — that part was true. The stack. Held.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rust, a mill yard seen through a chain-link gate with tall alders growing through the floorboards of the ruined building and a bare brick smokestack, no words
image.notes: The alders are real and forty feet. The rest of the sequence borrowed them.

panels.name: True
